x: Congratulations to our old friends the "Poly" on their third place in the "Southern," ably helped by our own Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who was 23rd.
Len Herbert did not find the going to his liking and finished no nearer than 19th closely followed by our Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who had ran steadily throughout to finish 23rd.

…ce and Martin Williamson, and it is pleasing to see these youngsters giving the senior members such a strong challenge. Jimmy Wood and Rene Howell (our Poly members) were also in the field and Bert Footer surprised a few by his forward running.…

Jimmy Wood, our Poly. member, caught and passed him but Len managed to hang on to second place with a time of 25.29 and handed over to Albert Frost who did well in putting up the fastest time for that leg which is now only just over 2 miles and his time of 10.51 kept us in second place.
Bill Lucas was third and Jimmy Wood gained a "standard" in seventh place. Harry Churcher easily retained his 2 miles' walk title in 14 mins. 35 secs.

Bragginton had run exceedingly well to beat such stalwarts as Ted Stimpson, Tom Carter and Jimmy Wood. Jack Shields, our Oxford University member, also ran well and deservedly won the handicap although he only beat Bragginton by the narrow margin of one second.
Ches Walker ran his best mile to date when gaining third place in the 1 mile final and he beat Jimmy Wood and also gained his Southern standard, which is of 4 mins. 28 secs.

Wilson and Jimmy Wood of the Poly, in the fast time of 9 min. 12.8 secs., which was a new ground record. We finished second in the team race to the Poly and final points for the trophy were:—1, Poly H., 31; 2, Walton A.C., 30; 3, Belgrave H., 20; 4, Finchley H., 16; 5, Thames Valley H., 12; 6, Highgate H., 5.

The latter, together with Jimmy Wood, who finished a good third this time, is a second-claim member and so not eligible for any championship award, but we are always pleased to welcome them to any of our club races.

Jack Bragginton just managed to beat Bill Lucas by the proverbial “hairbreadth” on the finishing line, and they were closely followed by Archie Bedford and Jimmy Wood, and the latter must think it strange to finish 15th and not score in the winning team.

Eric Bishop kept this position on the next stage and then Eddie Short lost one more place to Jim Peters of Essex Beagles and although Bill Lucas took us back into 3rd position our final runner Vern Blowfield found he could not make any impression on Jimmy Wood and Tommy Rowe who were in front of him.

Pirie, both just out of the junior stage, and he beat such men as Burfitt, Olney and Jimmy Wood. We also had Chas Walker and Ray Tooby qualifying for the final of this event and this speaks well for our strength at this distance.

Our team was minus Len Herbert and Len Adams, not to mention Jack Braughton and Jimmy Wood, who are eligible for this event, so that although we were pressed rather closely by Herne Hill Harriers, who had Greene, of Reading, assisting them, we can be quite satisfied with the actual result.

Archie Bedford finished third in the individual race with Vern Blowfield in fifth place, and then came Jimmy Wood 13th with Len Bishop 16th, and the latter just beat Tom Richards, the well known marathon runner.
Jimmy Wood was in fine form and all but sang one of his Brighton songs through the megaphone. The rail strike kept all the Herne Hill team away and a number of our own runners.

Jimmy Wood and Len Herbert were winners of the Surrey mile and 3 miles with a number of places gained in the field events. The Juniors showed equal success with Derek Burfitt and Arthur Bruce winning the Middlesex and Surrey miles respectively.
Jimmy Wood, our Poly. member, caught and passed him but Len managed to hang on to 2nd place and handed over to Albert Frost who did well in putting up the fastest time for that leg.
